mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of FEDFUNDS > 4% regimes, or the IC is positive with p < 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a softening labor market and reduced wage pressure, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening with deflationary pressures
failure_condition: IC for the combined proxy is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over a 5-year window, or 60-day returns are positive in >60% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in home sales (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a shift toward consumption-led growth, which historically precedes positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from manufacturing to services dominance
failure_condition: No significant correlation (p > 0.1) between the HOUST-INDPRO interaction and 20-day returns in the next 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness that lowers corporate earnings expectations and produces negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in each of the last three months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of INDPRO contraction regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a month following a decline in unemployment (UNRATE), it indicates accelerating inflation, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2% while CPIAUCSL increases by >2% in the subsequent month
regime_hint: accelerating inflation after labor market loosening
failure_condition: IC for the CPIAUCSL-UNRATE interaction is negative and statistically insignificant (p > 0.1) over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below 200,000 for two consecutive months suggests weakening labor demand, which tends to precede positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as markets price in recovery.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >75% of PAYEMS < 200,000 regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5% followed by a sustained period of no rate cuts (FEDFUNDS > 5% for 4 months) raises the real discount rate, which is expected to produce negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 5% regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (not available in the catalog – so this must be omitted) cannot be used. Instead: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not available – so use HOUST as proxy for consumption) and industrial production (INDPRO) suggests dual supply shocks, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >3% while INDPRO decreases by >1% in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: IC for the HOUST-INDPRO interaction is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over a 2-year horizon, or 60-day returns are positive in >50% of such events.
